# Clinics & Clinical Specialties 

## Clinics provide world-class care to our patients, establish patient registries and biorepositories to enable translational research in specific rheumatic diseases. 

In addition to general Rheumatology Clinic, the Stanford Division of Immunology and Rheumatology has specialized clinics in rheumatology-dermatology, cardiovascular disease, immuno-oncology, vasculitis, systemic lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, ultrasound, and sarcoidosis. 

Our specialized clinics not only provide world-class care to our patients, but also provide a foundation for clinical trials and biorepositories to enable translational research in specific rheumatic diseases.

 Fast-Track Inflammatory Arthritis Clinic Directors: Robert Fairchild, MD, PhD and Jison Hong, MD 

Our fast-track inflammatory arthritis clinic provides a rapid and comprehensive evaluation by inflammatory arthritis specialists and includes an “ultrasound first” clinical evaluation to understand and manage disease quickly. Our clinic is aligned with several arthritis-associated clinical and translational research studies.

 IgG4-Related Disease Clinic Director: Matthew Baker, MD, MS 

Our IgG4-related disease clinic cares for patients with IgG4-related disease, and the variety of ways in which the disease can affect the body. In addition to patient care, we have ongoing clinical trials at our center and laboratory-based research focused on better understanding disease mechanisms.

 Integrative Rheumatology Clinic Director: Neha Shah, MD 

Our integrative rheumatology clinic provides a holistic approach to care and management of rheumatic diseases, including the use of lifestyle changes, supplements, and mind-body medicine in addition to conventional rheumatologic care. We strive to identify root causes and employ shared decision-making to develop a personalized therapeutic plan. We also offer group visits.

IgG4 Related Disease Center | Henry Ford Health

# IgG4 Related Disease Center

 Henry Ford Health is home to one of only a few centers in the country dedicated to treating immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) related disease (IgG4-RD). Our program provides comprehensive care for patients with this complex condition. 

 

### Learn More About IgG4-Related Disease Care

For years, Henry Ford Health has been a respected leader in IgG4-related disease care. Our multidisciplinary team combines their expertise and knowledge to provide a treatment plan that meets all your needs. Here, you’ll discover what sets our clinic apart.

## Why choose Henry Ford Health for IgG4-related disease care?

IgG4-related disease is an inflammatory condition that can affect nearly any organ. This condition occurs when your immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissues. Because IgG4-RD can mimic other conditions, diagnosis can be challenging. Our experts specialize in these diseases and can provide you with the answers — and treatment — you deserve.

The Henry Ford Health difference:

- Leading-edge expertise: We are home to one of the nation’s leading dedicated IgG4-related disease centers. Our experts established the program in 2013. Since then, we have cared for one of the largest populations with IgG4-related disease in the U.S., including patients with complex, multi-organ involvement. 
- Coordinated care: Our team of specialists meets regularly to discuss your care. This collaboration helps avoid duplicate tests and delivers a treatment plan that addresses every aspect of your health.
- Advanced treatments: As part of a major academic medical center with an active research program, we offer clinical trials for IgG4-related disease. These trials give you options when standard treatments haven't worked, and you have access to care not widely available elsewhere.

IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program | Mass General Brigham

# IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program

The Mass General Brigham IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program is a national leader in the areas of clinical care and research for this recently recognized condition.

###### 617-726-7938

Call the IgG4-Related Systemic Disease Program at 617-726-7938.

6177267938

style palette-deep-blue

### Addressing IgG4-RSD as a systemic disease

IgG4-related systemic disease (IgG4-RSD) links a number of inflammatory disorders that previously were considered unrelated. Various clinical manifestations of the condition can cause fibrosis (the formation of excessive connective tissue) in a growing list of organs and tissues.

Mass General Brigham is one of the only U.S. health systems to recognize and treat IgG4-RSD as a systemic (i.e. whole-body) disease that affects multiple organs and tissues. Our research on this emerging disease has led to several important milestones, including:

- Pioneering a new treatment (rituximab)
- Establishing IgG4-RSD's link with thoracic aortitis and with Riedel's thyroiditis
- Organizing the first international symposium on IgG4-RSD

### What to expect

Many patients are referred to us by a pathologist who suspects IgG4-RSD.

Your doctor will review your medical history, perform a physical examination and, because information about IgG4-RSD is so hard to find, educate you about the disease. If necessary, we may recommend blood tests or review your biopsy specimen with a Mass General Brigham pathologist to confirm a diagnosis.

For many patients, receiving the diagnosis of IgG4-RSD comes as a relief. The condition often causes organ swelling, which previously may have been mistaken for a malignant tumor. Some patients have even undergone unnecessary surgery for this reason.

## CRMR Constitutif : CeRAINOM-IgG4

Maladies auto-immunes et auto-inflammatoires systémiques rares de l’adulte Nord, Nord-Ouest, méditerranée et Guadeloupe : pathologies infiltratives et fibrosantes associées aux IgG4 - CeRAiNOM-IgG4

- Filière de rattachement : Fai 2 r

- Patients concernés : Adultes

- Responsable médical Adultes: Pr Nicolas SCHLEINITZ

- Lieu Adultes pour la prise de RDV : Département de médecine interne et immunologie clinique Timone (7ème étage)

###### Description :

Le Centre de Référence Maladies auto-immunes et auto-inflammatoires systémiques et pathologies infiltratives et fibrosantes associées aux IgG4 est rattaché au département de médecine interne dirigé par le Professeur Nicolas SCHLEINITZ localisé à l’hôpital de la TIMONE.

Il a pour mission la coordination de la prise en charge (diagnostic et suivi) des patients atteints de pathologies auto-immunes (lupus, maladie de Sjogren, vascularites, sclérodermies, myopathies inflammatoires) et auto-inflammatoires.

Le centre est également labellisé "Maladie associée aux IgG4" pour son expertise nationale et a pour mission la coordination nationale d'un réseau pour le diagnostic, le suivi et la recherche clinique de la maladie associée aux IgG4 (Dijon, Bordeaux, Lyon, Paris et Lille).

Le CRMR fonctionne en lien étroit avec les CRMR CEREDIH Adulte et CERECAI du département de médecine interne.

Des consultations de transition sont réalisées avec les équipes de pédiatrie.

D'autre part, des consultations avancées sont réalisées dans d'autres CHU: Pr Ebbo au CH Bastia, Pr Schleinitz au CH Ajaccio, Dr Galicier à l'Institut Paoli Calmette et Dr Faucher au CH Toulon-La Seyne.

IgG4-Related Disease (IgG4-RD) - UChicago Medicine

## UChicago Medicine IgG4-Related Disease Clinical Consortium (IGGCC) 

UChicago Medicine is proud to offer the Midwest’s only dedicated clinical consortium for IgG4-Related Disease (IgG4-RD), a rare but serious inflammatory condition that can affect nearly every organ system in the body. IgG4-RD is characterized by immune system activation, organ inflammation and tissue fibrosis, which can lead to progressive and irreversible organ damage if left untreated. 

Our multidisciplinary consortium brings together experts from rheumatology, gastroenterology, nephrology, pathology, radiology, and other specialties to provide comprehensive, coordinated care. We specialize in accurate diagnosis through detailed evaluation of symptoms, imaging, blood tests, biopsies and treatment response, ensuring patients receive timely and precise diagnoses. 

Treatment plans are individualized and may include steroid therapy as a first-line approach, with access to emerging therapies and clinical research aimed at improving long-term outcomes and preventing disease relapse.

 Patients can access expert care at multiple convenient locations across the Chicago area, including: 

- Hinsdale
- Hyde Park
- River East
- Crown Point
- Orland Park 

UChicago Medicine’s IgG4-RD Clinical Consortium is committed to advancing understanding and treatment of this complex disease while providing patients with the highest level of expert care close to home.

For more information or to refer a patient, call 773-702-6140 (7737026140).

Namrata Setia, MD

Lindsay Alpert, MD

# Centre de compétence - Maladies auto-immunes et auto-inflammatoires systémiques rares de l'adulte Nord, Nord-Ouest, Méditerranée et Guadeloupe : pathologies infiltratives et fibrosantes associées aux IgG4

Adresse :
: Service de médecine interne CHU de Nantes 1 place Alexis Ricordeau 44093 Nantes

La maladie associée aux IgG4 est une maladie systémique rare, caractérisée par l’accumulation dans les tissus de cellules inflammatoires et par l’évolution de ces lésions vers la fibrose. Parmi les cellules inflammatoires sont retrouvés de nombreux plasmocytes (globules blancs) producteurs d’immunoglobulines de type G4, cet aspect particulier ayant donné le nom à la maladie. Elle peut atteindre de manière variable plusieurs organes, notamment les glandes salivaires et lacrymales, l’orbite, le pancréas, les voies biliaires, le rétropéritoine et les reins. 

Le traitement de cette pathologie repose, quand il est nécessaire, sur les corticoïdes parfois associés à d’autres médicaments immunosuppresseurs.
